full_judgment:
b. Cadastral Survey Plot No. 596 covering an area of 4.04 acres corresponding to State Acquisition plot No. 1334, area being 3.967 (tank). 1328/1502, being area 10 acres and plot Nos. 1334/1507, being area .01 had been suit property. 

 h. Suit tank was acquired by Additional Deputy Commissioner, (Revenue) Comilla. Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Comilla issued a Notice dated 1-10-1977 allegedly under sections 54(1) and 39(1) of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and Rules made thereunder stating that Government had acquired the suit tank under the provision of section 3 of The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and directed Abdur Razzak, predecessor of defendant-petitioner, to submit returns for assessment of compensation for the suit tank. Abdur Razzak, predecessor of defendant-petitioner and one Abdul Matin instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 467 of 1977 in the Court of Munsif, Sadar, Comilla now Assistant Judge for a declaration that order of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) acquiring suit tank is illegal and void. 

 i. Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Comilla and others as defendants put up contest against the suit on presentation of a written statement pressing into service contention that suit tank is a fishery and it was liable to be acquired by Government and Government legally acquired suit tank. 

 j. Learned Munsif dismissed suit adopting the view that suit tank was a fishery and it was liable to be acquired tinder section 3 of The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and it had been legally acquired by Government. 

 k. Feeling aggrieved by aforesaid decision of learned Munsif an appeal, being Title Appeal No. 154 of 1980, before learned District Judge, Comilla had been carried. Learned Subordinate Judge heard the appeal, allowed it, reversed decision rendered by learned trial Judge and decreed suit rendering decision that suit tank was not liable to be acquired under Ordinance No. 12 of 1960 and it was a tank excavated by human hand and, also, that tank was not acquirable under section 3 of The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 4. Plaintiff-opposite party put up resistance to Civil Revision Petition on laying a Counter-Affidavit controverting statements made in Revision Petition. Basic contention tabled in Counter-Affidavit is that question of res judicata is a mixed question of fact and law and res judicata can be decided at the time of trial. 

 i. Title of first-defendant-petitioner had been declared and possession had been confirmed on suit tank in Title Suit No. 136 of 1951 as well as title Suit No. 467 of 1977 and decision rendered in both the suits in respect of acquisition of Title on the part of predecessor of first-defendant-petitioner on the strength of Patta deed from Maharaja of Tripura had been confirmed by High Court Division as well as Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh and present suit is hit by the principle of res judicata and, also, of constructive res judicata and controversy, which was laid at rest finally by highest court of land i.e. Appellate Division, cannot be allowed to be re-opened by plaintiff-opposite party on laying a fraudulent, misconceived and fancy suit. 

 9. Doctrine of res judicata or constructive res judicata predominantly is a principle of equity, good conscience and justice. In Carl-Zeiss Stiftung vs Rayner and Keeler Ltd and others = (1967) The Law Reports: Appeal Cases 853 = (1966) 2 All ER it has been aptly stated by Lord Upjohn: The broader principle of res judicata is founded on twin principles. So frequently expressed in Latin that there should be an end to litigation and justice demands that the same party shall not be harassed twice for the same cause.
